§25 synthesis (opus 5f5ac58f + cursor 9376b50e converged). PICKS: (1) LOD driver = appW (apparent on-screen size = cellWidth_world × cameraScale), NOT raw camera scale — each node bands by its own readable size. (2) RESERVE-AT-DEEPEST packing: cell sized at deepest-LOD bbox, content-LOD only changes what is painted → footprint fixed (§22.1), zero reflow, overlap structurally impossible. (3) Two orthogonal mechanisms: BAND (paint, zoom-only-per-node) ⊥ DOMINANCE (focus-assist, viewport-relative, elevate+dim, no footprint change, no auto-pan). Double-click stays the committed/locked twin.

Ladder (appW @280px cell): L0 GLYPH <150 = handle+status ring + step constellation + volume cue only. L1 THREAD 150-320 = labels + step thread w/ 1-line titles + roster chips. L2 CARDS 320-560 = step mini-cards + subtask fan-out + clamped body. L3 READING >560 = full bodies+step cards+subtask bodies+rationale+pane link. Crossfade = opacity + 4px rise, ±10% hysteresis, NO geometry reflow.

§25.6 status emphasis is ORTHOGONAL to bands, multiplies at every LOD: in_progress = brighter + accent ring, pulses at L0 (eye-magnet = attract, never hijack wheel / never auto-pan); done ≈0.7 dim, restores toward 1.0 at L3 for comfortable history read; blocked = warning left border, normal opacity. Fractal: live task among tasks → live step among steps. One-key 'jump to active' fly-to + ping offered; auto-follow tail-mode default OFF.

§25.5 subtask volume = 'card-deck thickness' ONE object that unfolds: far(L0) = stacked-card depth silhouette (≤3 ghost layers, 3px offset) + ⊞N badge + done/total mini-bar; 0-subtask tasks stay FLAT so heavy ones pop. mid(L1) = peels to one-line roster chips (≤5 +k). near(L2) = fans out to subtask mini-cards in reserved super-cell (same object unfolding, 'fell INTO the stack'). reading(L3) = full subtask bodies + each subtask's own step thread (fractal). Never flatten all subtasks onto board.

ANDREY: want plans that 'flow out of' each other — a DIRECTED/typed lineage link (derived_from / spawned_by), persisting even after the source plan is archived & off-canvas, so we REMEMBER there was a related plan and the connection. ANDREY DECISION: Spec and Plan must be TWO DIFFERENT OBJECTS, not two views of one section set. Today: one Plan{sections} rendered as SPEC-node (prose view) + PLAN-node (structural view) — same sections, FE SectionNode variant. Target: a separate Spec entity with its OWN sections (prose), a Plan with its OWN task-bearing sections, connected by explicit typed edges (spec_section ↔ plan_section). Brainstorm §29 (data model/storage/migration, link model, coverage across two objects, optionality, CLI, canvas render generalizing §26 worlds).

ANDREY SHARPENED §29 model: SPEC=WHAT we want (intent), PLAN=HOW we do it (approach), TASK=concrete granular work on PLAN sections (+granular desc). Spec links ONLY to plan sections, NEVER to tasks. MILESTONES→rename 'work points' (work done / status change / brief what-updated; NOT history); attach to spec+plan+tasks; GROUPABLE like tasks. Spec+Plan+Tasks+work-points = ONE 'complete work'; multiple complete-works exist and LINK to each other (= plan lineage). NO legacy/migration (test-covered, no users) — manually reshape the current dogfood. Naming = separate brainstorm (names tentative).

Agent/CLI canvas focus = OFF-SCREEN SIGNAL (edge dot/glow toward the change + optional count, click to fly), NOT auto-pan. Applies to dominance(§25.3)/handoff(§27.4)/status(§25.6)/auto-pack. Layout: .codeterm/plans/<id>/meta.yaml + sections/<handle>/section.md (frontmatter+body) + tasks/<handle>/task.md + tasks/<handle>/events/<ulid>-<actor>.json (strides/status/assign/edit). specs same. mem: .codeterm/mem/items/<kind>/<id>.md + events. MERGE: ordinary git per-file (different entities = no conflict; same body edit = normal text conflict = correct human conflict); strides/status = append-only one-file-per-event → merge = file UNION, NO custom driver. Fold = snapshot + events by idempotent set-union + deterministic order. Scalar fields = Lamport tuple (logical_clock, actor, event_id) LWW ONLY where genuinely scalar; preserve competing body/text edits as git conflicts (NOT silent LWW). Single-writer per-worktree daemon; git = multi-writer transport; on merge/pull watcher folds + reindex (indexes discarded/rebuilt). Migration = one-time JSON→file-per-entity. Alts: pure-snapshot (status still conflicts), full-event-sourcing (every read needs fold), CRDT/Automerge (auto-merge but binary dep + parity work), Dolt (SQL+merge but heavy). Why not current big JSON: one large conflict surface (task arrays/milestones/spec_links/canvas collide).

ADOPT hybrid file-per-entity + append-only event log (git-bug-shaped). Files are source of truth, sqlite/vectors always derived. Extend §17 from bodies to the WHOLE structural record; kill the monolithic plan.json arrays (tasks[]/sections[]/milestones[]). One entity = one file, identity in filename (uuid/ULID), never two entities in one mutable array in one file -> git merges file-by-file, conflicts only on genuine same-entity same-field edits.

STRIDES = append-only event log. Per-task strides.jsonl with .gitattributes 'merge=union' (git built-in driver concatenates both branches' appended lines). Strides are immutable, ULID/time-prefixed ids. Deterministic fold = parse -> dedup by id -> sort by (lamport/ts,id) = the timeline. Two worktrees recording strides concurrently can NEVER conflict. One-file-per-stride is the fallback if union proves lossy. Strides target spec/plan/task -> shard log by target.

SLOW STRUCTURAL/PROSE = one .md per section/task with YAML frontmatter (all scalar fields in frontmatter, prose body below) — extends §17 verbatim, human-readable + PR-reviewable. plan.json shrinks to scalar meta only (id,title,status,owner,spec_refs) — NO tasks/sections/strides arrays. Slow mutable fields (status,priority,section_ids) = last-writer-wins by updated_at, lamport tie-break; high-frequency state (status transitions, canvas moves) optionally modeled as events + folded.

SQLITE INDEX + VECTORS ALWAYS DERIVED, gitignored, never in git (confirms §21). Rebuilt by existing reindex_missing on file-watcher rehydrate / post-merge. CHEAP + incremental: content-hash column skips unchanged bodies, only changed files re-embed; plan-scale FTS5/search-unit rebuild is sub-second. Daemon already watches .codeterm/ -> a git merge that changes files auto-triggers rehydrate+reindex; explicit post-merge hook is optional.

MERGE MECHANISM = git-native 3-way per-file + built-in 'merge=union' for *.jsonl logs. NO custom semantic merge driver, NO CRDT, NO Dolt. .gitattributes: '.codeterm/**/*.jsonl merge=union'. .gitignore: .codeterm/**/index.sqlite*, vectors, cache/. The whole point: the layout makes git's DEFAULT merge correct, so the diff stays human-readable and PR-reviewable. Custom driver would only be needed if we kept the monolith (we don't).

SINGLE-WRITER IS PER-WORKTREE; GIT IS THE CROSS-WORKTREE MERGE. Keep existing per-daemon serialized writer + atomic temp+rename + watcher rehydrate within a worktree (now cheaper). Across worktrees conflict resolution defers to git merge-time, trivial via file-per-entity + immutable events. No cross-process lock; git is the async CRDT.

MEM FACTS travel via the SAME model. Workspace-scoped facts = one .md per fact under .codeterm/mem/<area>/<id>.md (frontmatter id/kind/area/tags/source_path; body=fact). New facts=new files=no conflict; edits=LWW. file_sync.rs/source_path already does files->sqlite reindex so 'files are source, sqlite is cache' is half-built. GLOBAL/identity/peer facts stay home-sqlite NEVER git (matches scope split). Vectors derived.

MIGRATION = idempotent deterministic 'explode' on load (NO Date::now/Math.random — same rule as §17.3). Monolith plan.json -> task per tasks/<id>.md, stride per strides/<task>.jsonl, link/canvas one-per-file; plan.json becomes slim meta. Mirrors §17 hydrate_and_migrate migrated-flag; tasks/ dir + slim plan.json = already migrated -> re-run no-op.

REJECT CRDT (Automerge/Yjs): opaque binary docs DON'T git-diff/PR-review (binary-in-git again), heavy Rust dep, automerge-wasm in QuickJS breaks native+JS parity (arch rule #2). Conflict-freedom already achieved cheaper by immutable-event files. Only justified for real-time multi-cursor co-edit of ONE body, which §17 single-writer-per-body avoids.

REJECT Dolt (git-for-data): no Go runtime in Rust/Tauri, data lives in a SEPARATE dolt repo with own remotes -> does NOT travel inside the project's git branches/worktrees (the hard requirement), GitHub PRs show no plan diffs, replaces derived sqlite (contradicts §21). Escape hatch only if SQL-grade cell merge at scale is ever needed — plan/stride volume never needs it.

MERGE-STORAGE synth (opus 56957af8, 2/2 — converges w/ codex). The ONLY non-mergeable artifact today = monolithic <plan_id>.json (tasks[]+embedded strides). Bones exist (§17 .md = file-per-entity, §21 sqlite=derived) — finish decomposition. LAYOUT: plan.json=slim scalar meta; sections/<id>.md + tasks/<id>.md (frontmatter+body, extends §17); strides/<task>.jsonl (append-only ULID); links/+canvas/ one-file-per-entity; INDEX.md generated; sqlite+vectors gitignored. MERGE: git DEFAULT 3-way per-file + BUILT-IN merge=union for *.jsonl (.gitattributes) — NO custom driver, NO CRDT, NO Dolt. Two adds=two files=auto-merge; immutable stride events never conflict (fold=parse->dedup-by-id->sort ts,id). Concurrency: single-writer per-worktree; git IS cross-worktree merge. Mem: workspace facts=.md under .codeterm/mem/<area>/ (git-travel); global/identity stay home-sqlite. Migration: idempotent deterministic 'explode' on load (§17.3 migrated-flag). REJECTED CRDT/Dolt/pure-event-sourcing. SPIKE: verify git built-in union on EOF-append hunks before jsonl vs one-file-per-stride. BUILD ORDER: explode migration -> per-entity write path -> strides.jsonl+merge=union -> post-merge reindex -> mem workspace-fact files.
